concentration.text: Positive high-level results from the global SAFFRON Phase III trial: Tagrisso (osimertinib, 80mg once daily) plus Orpathys (savolitinib, 300mg twice daily) showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in both progression-free survival (primary endpoint) and overall survival (key secondary endpoint) versus doublet platinum-based chemotherapy in 338 patients with EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with high MET overexpression or amplification whose disease progressed after 1st- or 2nd-line Tagrisso. The trial ran in 230 centres across 29 countries, with patients prospectively selected using the high MET cut-offs identified in the SAVANNAH Phase II trial (IHC and FISH tests); safety was consistent with each medicine's known profile, and the data will be presented at a forthcoming medical meeting and shared with global regulatory authorities. The combination is already approved in China (SACHI Phase III) and has a temporary authorisation in Switzerland (SAVANNAH). The company estimates 34% of tumours develop high MET overexpression or amplification after progression on a third-generation EGFR-TKI. Orpathys is jointly developed with HUTCHMED and commercialised by AstraZeneca. Tagrisso is approved as monotherapy in more than 120 countries and with chemotherapy in more than 80 countries, and has treated more than one million patients. The company calls SAFFRON the first global Phase III trial to show significant PFS and OS benefits in this setting (company claim). — SAFFRON PFS and OS both statistically significant (high-level results, no numbers released); 338 patients, 230 centres, 29 countries; 34% develop high MET after a third-generation EGFR-TKI; Tagrisso monotherapy approved in more than 120 countries, with chemotherapy in more than 80

slots.supply_status: Component supply is tight across the board: lead times are stretching and MOSFETs in particular are short, though Delta's purchasing scale and supplier relationships keep demand largely fulfilled. Memory was the hardest hit - one business unit could not secure memory volumes at workable prices, so it switched designs to second sources and expects H2 shipments to normalize and catch up the backlog without a loss. On wide-bandgap devices (silicon carbide, gallium nitride) Delta works early and closely with the most important suppliers, keeps talking with them continuously and gets early access to new products, but will not disclose any agreements; it is also broadening its supply chain, including Taiwanese supplier options. Supplier price increases will be negotiated and passed to customers where the business model allows, with a timing lag.

concentration.text: Market position and mix shift: the company estimates its Q2 2026 global CCL share at 30% in package CCL, 22% in flexible CCL (single and double sided) and 16% in halogen-free CCL. slots.guidance: 2026 business plan (annual report): the company calls communications optics its core strategic segment. In 2026 it will focus on ramping optical isolator capacity and yield (expanding capacity by optimising lines and adding staff), move WDM filters, Z-block assemblies, prisms and optical assemblies from sampling to volume shipment and raise their share of communications revenue, and invest in components for 1.6T/3.2T modules (higher-performance WDM filters, more integrated and miniaturised Z-blocks) and in Faraday rotator materials (crystal preparation). It will advance the Nanchang base, adjusting the expansion pace for isolators and spin-coated filters to demand; in imaging it will defend its spin-coated filter share and build the phone micro-prism line. It says global Faraday rotator supply is tight and China's rare-earth export controls widen the gap; it has contingency plans and is cultivating diversified supply. Management says it is confident and that the dual-engine pattern is expected to lift overall results to a new level.
slots.supply_status: Management (IR record; general manager, CFO): Faraday rotators come mainly from overseas, with Japanese makers among the main global suppliers; isolators are currently made mainly with overseas mainstream suppliers' rotators. The company has long-term cooperation with core upstream suppliers; purchasing and production scheduling are normal and operations have not been directly hurt by the policies so far. It hedges rotator price rises through long-term volume and price agreements and stocking, and does not grow rotator crystals itself, though a subsidiary slices, polishes and coats them. Some core customers set terms in mid- to long-term orders, but not all orders are price-locked.
slots.next_catalyst: Nanchang production base project 59.09% invested; ready-for-use date May 31, 2026
